# Survey grid cases: the inputs to Mission Planner's Grid.CreateGrid, Grid.CreateCorridor and
# Grid.CreateRotary for the golden outputs in golden/, and to crates/mp-mission/tests/
# grid_vectors.rs, corridor_vectors.rs and rotary_vectors.rs. Regenerate the goldens with
# tools/csharp-reference/regen-grid.sh after any change here; see README.md.
#
#   polygon <name> <lat>,<lng> ...          vertices in drawing order, degrees
#   case <name> <polygon> [<param>=<value> ...]        CreateGrid, golden/<name>.csv
#   corridor <name> <polygon> [<param>=<value> ...]    CreateCorridor, golden/corridor/<name>.csv
#   rotary <name> <polygon> [<param>=<value> ...]      CreateRotary, golden/rotary/<name>.csv
#
# Parameters are the generator's own names (ExtLibs/Utilities/Grid.cs:354, :55 and :196); a
# corridor's polygon is the centre line, which Grid.cs also calls `polygon`. One that is left out
# takes the value GridUI gives it on a fresh install - the list is in
# tools/csharp-reference/MpGrid.cs - including the angle, which GridUI sets to the bearing of the
# polygon's longest side.

# --- Canberra, around the SITL home (-35.363261, 149.165230): UTM zone 55 south -------------------

# --- frames the C# chooses by the first vertex ----------------------------------------------------
# A polygon is projected in the zone and hemisphere of its first vertex (PointLatLngAlt.cs:296), so
# the same area can be laid out in two frames.

# ==================================================================================================
# Rotary: Grid.CreateRotary (Grid.cs:196-310) flies the polygon's outline, then the outline inset

# HomeLocation, clockwise_laps, match_spiral_perimeter, laps and Grid.StartPointLatLngAlt reach the
# pattern; spacing is overwritten with 0 and the rest is never read.
# ==================================================================================================

# and longitudes happen to put it: these integer paths are exactly collinear and touch, so they
# reach its joins, splits, holes and the partitioning sort. Positive deltas, which CreateRotary
# never passes, take the offset's other branch (clipper.cs:4801).
#
#   path <name> <x>,<y> ...                             ClipperLib.IntPoint coordinates
#   offset <name> <path>[+<path>...] <delta>[/<delta>...]
# ==================================================================================================
